liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Mississippi Half-Step Uptown Toodeloo** (1 review): Jerry sounds slightly weak, though the band plays at full strength; Garcia's playing in the 8:45–9:30 stretch is showy [11]
- **Franklin's Tower** (1 review): Many incomplete musical spaces despite full backing vocals; Brent will have to fill some of those holes [11]
- **Estimated Prophet** (1 review): The Estimated Prophet into Eyes jam is the reviewer's highlight, and the second set is especially good [17]
- **Eyes Of The World** (1 review): The jam in Eyes is singled out as strong enough to justify the whole show [13]
- **Stella Blue** (1 review): The band took a frenzied crowd from Truckin' down to absolute silence during Stella Blue, a dramatic moment [14]

## The recordings

- **gd79-05-04.glassberg.vernon.18878.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): audience recording; 22 songs; 173 min; rated 4/5 by 9 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls this audience recording very fine for its period; Glassberg's taping is said to sound as good as the live show did; Reviewer finds the recording quality unremarkable [10][13][14][19]
- **gd1979-05-04.nak700.glassberg.86389.flac24**: audience recording; 22 songs; 174 min; rated 3.67/5 by 3 [2]. Said about its sound: A crowd section is missing between disc 1 tracks 6 and 7, smoothed with a crossfade [2]
- **gd1979-05-04.177538.nak700.glassberg.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 22 songs; 177 min [3]
- **gd1979-05-04.sonyecm.walker-scotton-miller.89120.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 178 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [5]. Said about its sound: Brent's organ sounds creamier than it later would, adding texture absent from Keith's playing [20]
- **gd1979-05-04.nak700.glassberg.motb.84825.sbeok.flac16**: source not stated; 22 songs; 174 min; rated 3.25/5 by 4 [6]. Said about its sound: Sounds nice, with the piano high and very audible in the mix [18]

## Around the show

- No encore happened because someone threw a shirt at Bobby, who had to shake it off his playing hand [10]
- Heavy rain fell and the band arrived late, yet the mood held; locals met deadhead culture for the first time [12]
- Outside, Southern and Northeast heads reunited with West Coast diehards amid buses carrying VW Buses, stir fry, bracelets and bartering [12]
- Reviewer believes they threw the shirt onto Weir as he played, which ended the night without an encore [16]
- This was the band's first appearance at Hampton Coliseum, later released as a 2LP set [25]
- With Brent, the band sounds tighter and more cohesive, with more kick in overdrive than with Keith [19]
- The band is more aggressive than at any point since 1971, in the context of late-'70s punk and new wave [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd79-05-04.glassberg.vernon.18878.sbeok.shnf**: taped by Barry Glassberg; source: Audience Recording [1]
- **gd1979-05-04.nak700.glassberg.86389.flac24**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by A. Egert; source: Audience FOB Recording Media: Maxell UD-XLII 90 min. Lineage: Nakamichi CM700's > Sony 158SD > MAC [2]. Also: A tape flip at the end of Drums loses an unknown amount, crossfaded into Space [2]
- **gd1979-05-04.177538.nak700.glassberg.menke.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by Bob Menke, Charlie Miller, Scott Clugston; source: Barry Glassberg's Master Audience Cassettes: Nakamichi 700 mics > Sony TC-158SD (Maxell UDXL II) [3]
- **gd1979-05-04.sonyecm.walker-scotton-miller.89120.flac16**: taped by Joani Walker; transferred by Charlie Miller; source: (FOB) Sony ECM-250 -> Cassette Master (Sony TC-158/Maxell UDXL-II90) [5]. Also: Source is Joani Walker and Paul Scotton's tapes, patched from Nakamichi 700 cassette master via DAT; patch by Robert Wagner and Glassberg, pitch-adjusted [5]
- **gd1979-05-04.nak700.glassberg.motb.84825.sbeok.flac16**: taped by Barry Glassberg; transferred by A. Egert and SIRMick; source: Nakamichi CM700's > Sony 158SD > MAC [6]. Also: Barry Glassberg recorded this from the mouth of the beast area, within the first 15 rows of floor seating [18]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by The Second Disc: ["Weird Scenes Inside" Rhino's Record Store Day Slate - The Second Disc](https://theseconddisc.com/2014/04/10/weird-scenes-inside-rhinos-record-store-day-slate/) [26]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Hampton Coliseum - May 4, 1979](https://www.dead.net/show/may-4-1979) [27]
- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Hampton Coliseum - May 4, 1979](https://www.dead.net/show/may-4-1979) [28]
